The paper presents an active acoustic illusion technique using monopole control sources and error sensors.
The technique enables stealth and subterfuge applications by misrepresenting the acoustic fields due to scattering by a rigid object.
20 control sources and 40 error sensors are used in the experiments.
The first stage of the control strategy is to completely remove the total acoustic field at the error sensor locations (sound cancellation).
The second stage of the control strategy is to generate the desired acoustic illusion (sound reproduction).
The frequency of the incident plane wave and monopole source excitation is 200 Hz.
The radius of the original cylinder in the experiments is a.
The radius of the larger cylinder in the experiments is 2a.
The distance by which the larger cylinder is shifted in the experiments is a.
The technique can generate illusions that misrepresent both the size and location of the object.
The technique can generate illusions that actively manipulate the total field.
The control sources are arranged circumferentially around the cylinder.
The error sensors are arranged circumferentially around the cylinder.
The technique uses a multichannel control configuration.
The Helmholtz equation governs the acoustic domain for time-harmonic responses.
